title: Cover a finite-length Hilbert orbit by one positive trace-class operator
statement: For an absolutely continuous unit-norm h:[0,ell]->H with ||h'||<=1 a.e., extend constantly to ell+1. Gamma=2 integral_0^(ell+1)(|h><h|+|h'><h'|) ds dominates |h(s)><h(s)| for every s in [0,ell] and tr Gamma<=2+4ell.

requires: Supplied real or complex Hilbert curve of finite length in the stated unit-speed parameter
provides: Single positive trace-class rank-one majorant for the entire supplied curve
Explicit trace budget without selecting finitely many time samples
assumptions: All test vectors are covered by the operator inequality
ell=0 is the constant-vector case; arbitrary speed needs justified reparametrization
costs: Trace upper bound 2+4ell; not a free physical calibration
contract.units: h normalized, s Hilbert arclength, ell finite; abstract operator trace
contract.obstruction: Does not prove Gaussian speed, 1+NT necessity, field projection or physical advantage.
